## QUESTION

1. __Take time to get to know your data.__ Based on some initial exploration, identify 3 variables in the dataset you think will have strong predictive ability for determining if a house was built before 1980. Explain/justify the reasoning behind your guesses (for example with plots).

Also, by looking at the target (before1980), I'm getting a lot of zeroes there too, which means most (if not all) of this data shows houses built after 1980._

target = df.select("before1980")

1. __Build a classification model labeling houses as being built “before 1980” or “during or after 1980”.__ Your goal is to reach or exceed 90% accuracy. Report your final model choice and any other model parameters you may have tweaked (train-test split ratio, tuning parameters, etc).  

_My final model choice was the Random Forest Classifier. My accuracy started off very low, so the only tweaks I made was adding more and more features for the model to learn from. I think it was starved for information._

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
# Don't forget, you need another import statement to import the desired ML model from sklearn
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

# You can name the 4 objects anything you like. These names are pretty standard though
x_train, x_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(feature, target, test_size=0.1, random_state=20)

# You can use these two commands to check the size of the 4 objects and verify they meet your expectations
print(x_train.shape, y_train.shape)
print(x_test.shape, y_test.shape)

from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report
rf_classifier = RandomForestClassifier() #define the model
rf_classifier.fit(x_train, y_train) #fit the model on the training data

rf_pred = rf_classifier.predict(x_test)

print(classification_report(y_test, rf_pred))

```
